forecasts.reason: Cutting 0.5 epoch saves about 5% of time (≈0.33 s) for about 0.05–0.2 pp. The true tip is only about 0.1–0.2 pp over the bar, so seeds 0–2 land near 0.753 either way. Held-out seeds are needed, and the −0.5 point probably falls just under 0.7545.

The pixel fraction drops from 0.755 to 0.723, which saves about 0.25 s. The accuracy cost should be smaller than E018's because the 3×3 regime is kept, but probably not zero. A 0.1–0.3 pp loss eats the margin.
Time-neutral. The averaging is already worth about 1 pp, and pulling harder mid-run also slows progress, so the net effect is probably within noise rather than +0.3 pp.
Every LS and other hyperparameter nudge so far has landed inside noise (E013). A per-phase LS split is unlikely to buy 0.2 pp.

Diagnostic with no recipe change, so a rerun reproduces the tip. A rough FLOP budget (about 1e15 FLOP in about 6 s) implies high conv efficiency, so the profile should show at least 90 TFLOP/s at 32 px. The group-2 shortfall would then come from non-conv and fixed costs.

With the main step count matched, main-net compute is unchanged. On top of that come the proxy forward/backward, augmenting twice the data, and topk/gather, so time rises 5–20%. Any accuracy gain would have to be converted into epoch cuts later, so this run cannot show the 5% time cut that H2.4.1 requires.

cruxes: What is the tip's true held-out mean (seeds 3–12)? If it is at least 0.756, the −0.5 epoch and group 2 at 352 trims become feasible; if it is about 0.754, every trim needs a time-neutral accuracy gain first.
Does any time-neutral lever (EMA schedule, BN recalibration, per-phase LS) actually give at least 0.2 pp? At about 6 s/pp, every 0.1 pp it buys funds about 0.6 s of cuts.
Does a 26 px middle phase cost near-zero accuracy? If so, the 3×3-regime boundary, not pixel count, sets the price of resolution, and cheaper schedules open up.
structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E021, unchanged in substance.

**Time budget.** Time ≈ 0.6 s fixed + 7.8 s × pixel fraction. Systems levers are spent. Cutting a FLOP returns only about half its share as time.

**Accuracy.** The tip's true mean is about 0.754–0.755, so the binding constraint is margin, not efficiency.

**Exchange rates.**
- Epochs and group-2 width cost about 6 s per pp.
- Last-group width and dropping a resolution phase cost about 1.6 s per pp or worse.

**What would help.** First buy margin with a time-neutral accuracy gain, then spend it on −0.5 epoch.

**Noise.** The 3-seed SE is about 0.17 pp, and kernel reshuffles add more.
